about.bio: Engineering student at CPE Lyon and full-stack developer apprentice at UBIKAP, I am passionate about web development and building efficient digital solutions. With hands-on experience in Angular and Node.js, I strive to design performant, maintainable, and user-centered applications.

items.title: Ubikap SaaS Platform
items.description: A business platform I maintain and keep improving at Ubikap. I handle the day-to-day maintenance, fix blocking bugs, and build new features on my own. I've come to know the product inside out, and I make sure the code stays clean and readable so the whole team can step in easily.

items.title: CPE Notes
items.description: Grade tracking app I built so I don't have to log into MyCPE every day. A script automatically fetches my grade reports and shows them in a dashboard with per-unit and per-year averages. It also has a calendar synced with my schedule, a simulator to test grades before exams, manual editing when the scraper misses something, and Discord notifications as soon as a new grade comes in. The backend is Node.js with Express and Prisma, the frontend is Angular, and everything runs in Docker on my VPS with PostgreSQL.

items.title: IT Department ERP
items.description: An ERP built in a team of twenty to handle the day-to-day of an IT department. It covers emails, class schedules, training, internships, apprenticeships, grades, and attendance. Everything is kept in one tool instead of being spread across several spreadsheets and apps.

items.title: Eduquiz
items.description: A flashcard revision site inspired by Quizlet. You build a deck of cards on a topic, then drill yourself by flipping them one by one. It was my first project in PHP and JavaScript, and it mainly taught me how a website with a database and user accounts actually works.

items.title: Wizard Toolbox
items.description: An online toolbox I built for my own needs, leaning on AI to move faster. It brings together a file converter, an image and PDF compressor, text utilities, an encoder, and a code formatter. Everything is free and runs straight in the browser, nothing to install.

items.title: Portfolio 2026
items.description: This portfolio, which I keep updating for my internship search abroad while studying engineering. I spent time on the design and the animations, and it's available in three languages. It's also a playground for trying out things I use in class or at work.

items.title: Portfolio 2025
items.description: A portfolio I made for a course at the IUT. It covers the skills I picked up throughout my Computer Science BUT, with a more academic layout and a simpler design. It got me comfortable with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript before moving on to bigger projects.

items.title: Portfolio 2024
items.description: My very first portfolio, made in my second year of BUT to land a first internship. It's simple, but it taught me the basics of web layout and design. I keep it online to show where I started from.

items.title: Transport Decision Support
items.description: A small Java tool to compute routes between cities using graph theory. You enter a start point and a destination, and the program compares the possible paths to find the shortest one. A class project that made me look at graph algorithms more closely.

items.title: Directory Management
items.description: A C program that manages a contacts directory stored in a CSV file. You can look someone up by name, add a record, edit it, or delete it. A short but useful project that got me working with data structures and file handling in C.

items.title: Sorting Algorithms
items.description: A Java implementation of several sorting algorithms: bubble sort, merge sort, insertion sort, and selection sort. I compared how fast they run on lists of different sizes to see which ones still hold up as the data grows. A good exercise for understanding algorithm complexity.

items.title: Blog
items.description: A full blog built with PHP and MySQL where each post has an author and can be published or taken down depending on permissions. There's an admin area with accounts to manage the content, all backed by a MySQL database. It's the project that taught me the most about user accounts and sessions.

items.title: Power BI Dashboards
items.description: Power BI dashboards built for a business project: tracking sales, margins, and costs, with charts that filter based on what you select. The goal was to move past raw data and give a readable overview so decisions could be made faster.
